Commands/steps used:

1. Read `./b4w.ps1 help`, `skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md` (full), `references/attach.md`, `references/browser-modes.md`, and `AGENTS.md`; used `--help attach`, `--help close`, `--help disconnect`, `--help browsers`.
2. Recorded baseline with `./b4w.ps1 --version`, `status`, `list`, and the scenario's exact PowerShell helper (CIM process counts + `Get-NetTCPConnection` on 9222/8088 + `Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1:9222`).
3. Ran `./b4w.ps1 attach --extension msedge`; captured the ordered output and timing.
4. Ran `list` and `tab-list`, then re-measured the footprint/ports.
5. Ran the second unnamed `attach --extension msedge`, captured exit code 1 and the message; re-ran `list` and footprint.
6. Ran `disconnect`, then `list`, footprint/ports; inspected the backend log (`doctor log pulsar`) to see what happened to the session tab.
7. Ran `close` for cleanup, then final `list` and footprint.

Decisions/workarounds:

- Used the dev wrapper invocation exclusively (`./b4w.ps1 …`), as required.
- Used PowerShell only for OS-level process/port checks; no browser automation/CDP tools were used.
- Treated the pre-existing files in the run scratch directory (from an earlier attempt, 22:26–22:40) as untrusted and re-baselined live state. There were no live sessions or Browser4-managed browsers, so results are unaffected.
- Avoided UI Automation to count Edge windows/tabs; the scenario's process/port evidence plus CLI output was used instead. This observability gap is recorded as an issue.

## C/D. Issues Found and Overall Assessment



**Overall:** The core attach/footprint workflow is reliable and well-documented once found; the remaining friction is in lifecycle messaging and post-disconnect observability rather than in the attach mechanism itself.

issues.title: Normal extension disconnect logs an internal closeTab CancellationException and cannot confirm the tab closed

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1) ./b4w.ps1 attach --extension msedge
2) ./b4w.ps1 disconnect
3) ./b4w.ps1 doctor log pulsar, then search for 'closeTab' near the disconnect time.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Disconnect closes the session tab cleanly. A debugger detach that is the consequence of the tab being removed should be treated as success, with no exception stack trace, and the tab outcome should be confirmed before the CLI reports success.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The CLI prints success and exits 0, but the backend log at 22:45:04 shows: WARN ai.platon.pulsar.chrome.PulsarBrowser - WebDriverException: closeTab ... Caused by: ChromeServiceException: closeTab timed out or failed: get ... Caused by: CancellationException at ExtensionChromeService.handleEvent, triggered by 'Debugger detached from tab 1439683073'. The detach (caused by the tab removal) cancels the pending chrome.tabs.remove request, and the exception is swallowed into a WARN while the session is reported as successfully deleted.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: ExtensionChromeService cancels all pending requests when chrome.debugger.onDetach fires. closeTab's own chrome.tabs.remove causes that detach before its response arrives, so awaitAndCleanup's future is cancelled and reported as a close failure. The caller (PulsarBrowser.doClose) only logs the exception, and no post-close check verifies the tab is actually gone, so a genuine close failure would also be silent.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: Dependency pulsar-browser-4.11.25.jar (not this checkout): ai.platon.pulsar.chrome.protocol.transport.ExtensionChromeService.closeTab (ExtensionChromeService.kt:127) and awaitAndCleanup (:310-313). Backend call site: browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/session/PulsarSessionManager.kt:1953 (closeSession).

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Treat a CancellationException/detach that arrives while closeTab is awaiting chrome.tabs.remove as success when the target tab id is no longer present; log at DEBUG instead of WARN with a stack trace.
- If the tab is still present, surface a real failure to the CLI instead of exiting 0.
- Return the tab outcome (closed / still open / unknown) in the close/disconnect response so the CLI can report it.
- Add a regression test for the onDetach-vs-tabs.remove race on extension-session close.

issues.title: close is described as 'Close the browser'; disconnect text says 'Browser4 Chrome Extension' and that tabs remain, which is misleading for an Edge attach

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 --help close
./b4w.ps1 attach --extension msedge
./b4w.ps1 disconnect

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Help and messages should describe detach semantics for attached sessions, name the actual browser family (Microsoft Edge), and distinguish the session-driven tab from the user's own tabs.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: --help close prints only 'Close the browser' (the main help row is the same), which sounds like it will terminate Edge. After a successful Edge attach, disconnect prints 'Disconnected from Browser4 Chrome Extension. Your browser tabs and the extension remain active.' even though the session is 'Extension (Microsoft Edge 155.0.0.0)' and the backend attempted chrome.tabs.remove on the session tab (attach.md says the driven tab is removed). Only `disconnect --help` mentions detach semantics.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The close command description is a legacy generic string, and the disconnect success message is hardcoded and family-agnostic. The wording does not separate the user's tabs from the tab the session drove, and the documentation's close table and message use different mental models.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:818 (close description); cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:4040 (disconnect message); skills/browser4-cli/references/attach.md:417 (documented close semantics).

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Align the close description with the disconnect alias, e.g. 'Close the current session (attached sessions detach; the external browser keeps running)'.
- Make the disconnect message name the actual browser/extension family and state the tab outcome from the backend report.
- Use 'Browser4 Extension' instead of 'Chrome Extension' when the connected family is Edge.

issues.title: No-session close/disconnect prints an error-styled 'Session required' block with irrelevant open/goto advice and a .exe hint, but exits 0

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
After ./b4w.ps1 disconnect (or with no session at all), run:
./b4w.ps1 close
./b4w.ps1 disconnect

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A neutral message such as 'No attached session to disconnect', exit 0, and optionally an attach --extension hint.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Prints '🔐 Session required', suggests `browser4-cli.exe open <url>`, `goto <url>` and `list`, and exits 0. The block looks like a failure, the suggestions do not apply to close/disconnect, and browser4-cli.exe is not the dev-wrapper invocation the user typed.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: handle_close falls back to the generic no_active_session_message() guard when no session is stored, then returns Ok(()) so the process exits 0. cli_binary_name() uses argv[0], which under the wrapper is browser4-cli.exe, so the guidance bypasses ./b4w.ps1 without saying so.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:4010-4023 (handle_close); cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:697-724 (cli_binary_name / no_active_session_message).

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Give close/disconnect their own no-session message and skip the generic session-required guidance.
- When running under ./b4w.ps1 or ./b4w.sh, print the wrapper invocation (have the wrapper export it) instead of browser4-cli.exe.
- Document the intended exit code for a no-op close (0 is reasonable, but the output must not look like an error).

issues.title: attach --extension prints no page/tab identity despite attach.md promising it, and after disconnect there is no CLI way to see what remained

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 attach --extension msedge
Compare output with skills/browser4-cli/references/attach.md ('After a successful attach, the CLI prints the target browser's real current page URL').
./b4w.ps1 tab-list
./b4w.ps1 disconnect
./b4w.ps1 tab-list

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A successful attach should print the target page/tab identity (as documented), and the user should be able to determine which tab was created and whether disconnect closed or left it.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Success output ends at 'Connected browser: Microsoft Edge 155.0.0.0' and 'Session ready: <id>' with no URL or tab GUID. While attached, tab-list shows only the session's own about:blank tab; after disconnect the CLI has no session and cannot show the tab's fate. The scenario's 'record what remains' step therefore cannot be answered from the CLI.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The extension-attach success branch prints only the browser name and session id; the page-URL output exists only on the CDP path. The disconnect message is a fixed sentence rather than a report of the tab outcome.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:2829-2872 (extension attach success path); skills/browser4-cli/references/attach.md ('Endpoint verification').

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Print the bound tab's GUID and URL after 'Session ready' for extension attaches.
- Include the tab close outcome (closed / left open, with GUID) in disconnect output and --json.
- Document the extension attach's new-tab scope next to the attach help text.

issues.title: attach --extension is not surfaced in the top-level Quick Start or Common workflows

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 help and search for 'attach'.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The 'use my own browser' workflow should be discoverable from the top-level help, e.g. under Common workflows.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: attach appears only once in the entire top-level help, in the [Browsers] command table. The Quick Start box and Common workflows omit it, so a first-time user must already know the term 'attach' or browse the Browsers category. --help attach and references/attach.md are thorough once found.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The top-level help hero sections list only high-frequency navigation/extraction commands; the attach workflow is only in the category table and deep-dive docs.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs (command registry / help metadata) and the top-level help renderer that builds the Quick Start and Common workflows sections.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a 'Use my own browser' line to Common workflows: attach --extension <channel>.
- Mention the Web Store extension prerequisite in that line.
- Consider listing attach in the Quick Start box since it is a headline feature.

issues.title: Repeat-attach refusal suggests --cdp chrome, a different transport from the failed --extension attach

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: With the unnamed Edge extension session active, run ./b4w.ps1 attach --extension msedge again.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The guidance should repeat the same transport, e.g. browser4-cli -s myname attach --extension msedge.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The message's example is 'browser4-cli -s myname attach --cdp chrome'; only a terse trailing 'Hint: browser4-cli -s <name> attach --extension' names the right transport. The suggested CDP path requires a debug port that extension users deliberately avoided.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: check_unnamed_slot_free hardcodes a generic example and does not know which transport (extension vs cdp) and channel were attempted.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:796 (check_unnamed_slot_free).

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Build the example from the attempted transport and channel, e.g. `-s myname attach --extension msedge`.
- Keep one consistent hint instead of a generic example plus a second appended hint.
